meta.source: DOW = Getting Started With Observability for Distributed Systems (DZone Refcard, 2021, 7 pp.); OTW = Getting Started With OpenTelemetry (DZone Refcard, 2021, 7 pp.)
meta.page_convention: PDF page = printed number (1-7). Page 2 of each PDF is an ad with no technical content.
meta.labels: rules = stated in the sources (with page); not_in_book = NOT in the sources: can only be said as [inference], [extrapolation] or [DATED].

monitoring_vs_observability.name: Monitoring vs observability
monitoring_vs_observability.summary: Monitoring obtains state from predefined measurements for known problems; observability measures understanding of state from multiple outputs and must be designed in from the start.
rules: Monitoring: state from predefined measurements, detects a known set of problems (DOW p.3)
Observability: understanding of state from multiple outputs; a capability designed in during initial construction, like reliability and security (DOW p.3)
Monitoring tells you when something is wrong; observability tells you why; monitoring is a subset (DOW p.3)
Everyone's responsibility, as with DevSecOps (DOW p.3)
not_in_book: Formal definition of controllability/observability from control theory

pillars.name: Pillars: logs, metrics, traces (3) and five pillars
pillars.summary: The text mentions three pillars (logs, metrics, traces) on p.3 and five on p.5 (three for collection, alerting and graphing for interpretation). Figure 2 uses Monitoring, Logging, Tracing.
rules: Observability complements monitoring with three pillars: logs, metrics, traces (DOW p.3)
Five pillars: three for collection and two for interpretation (DOW p.5)
The three data types work together (DOW p.4)
not_in_book: Events/profiles as additional pillars (note: Fig. 2 mentions Profiling as a step, without detail)

metrics.name: Metrics
metrics.summary: Numeric measurements of state; with tags they can be grouped; in OTel they are aggregated in the emitting application and collected at fixed intervals.
rules: Numeric measurements, tags allow grouping and querying, good for trends (DOW p.4)
Anyone can create a metric (DOW p.4)
In OTel: aggregated in the emitting application, intervals from 1 s to 1 day, basis for alerts and automated actions (OTW p.4)
Examples: request rate, latency per histogram bucket, bandwidth usage (OTW p.4)

logs.name: Logs and log policy
logs.summary: Immutable timestamped records; three formats; global log policy and tag management; a collector centralizes.
rules: Immutable and timestamped; plaintext, structured, or binary (DOW p.4)
Global policy: format and flow, verbosity per environment, transformations (DOW p.6)
Tags to correlate metric and event; collector reads, transforms, centralizes; compression and archiving (DOW p.6)
In OTel: logs standalone or attached to spans (OTW p.4)
not_in_book: Correlating log with trace via trace_id in the log

traces.name: Traces and spans
traces.summary: Trace = lifecycle of a request across services; span = operation with duration, errors, and a reference to its parent; tree with a root span.
rules: A trace represents the request lifecycle in the distributed system (DOW p.4)
A span records duration, errors, and a reference to the parent span (OTW p.4)
Spans form a tree with a root; they need a name, unique ID, and trace ID (OTW p.5)
SpanKind describes relationships such as synchronous calls and helps visualize latency (OTW p.5)
Unique identifier at each step to correlate (DOW p.6)
not_in_book: SpanKind values other than SERVER and INTERNAL in the example

context_propagation.name: Context API and context propagation
context_propagation.summary: OTel injects context (trace ID, span ID, state) into headers and extracts it in the receiving service; allows user-defined properties.
rules: Context includes trace ID, span ID, and the current span's state (OTW p.5)
Injection into headers and extraction at the receiver = context propagation (OTW p.5)
User-defined properties (e.g., user ID, region) can be attached (OTW p.5)
not_in_book: W3C traceparent format (DOW p.7 only lists the link)

sdk_tracing.name: Tracing SDK: Tracer Provider, sampling, processors
sdk_tracing.summary: Tracer Provider creates traces and configures processors, sampling, IDs, and limits; the SDK can filter/sample and export to multiple destinations.
rules: The SDK is the bridge between API and export; filters or samples; multiple destinations (OTW p.3)
Tracer Provider configures processors, sampling, IDs, and limits (OTW p.4)
Span processors in a pipeline in registration order (OTW p.5)
BatchSpanProcessor groups spans before the exporter (OTW p.5)
not_in_book: Tail-based/head-based sampling strategies and sampler types (always_on, parent-based, ratio)

collector.name: Collector: receivers, processors, exporters, pipelines
collector.summary: Vendor- and language-agnostic alternative; YAML pipelines connect receivers, processors (order matters), and exporters.
rules: Vendor- and language-independent (OTW p.3)
Receivers listen on ports or pull; processors enrich/transform in sequence (order matters); exporters send to backends, with multiple destinations (OTW p.3)
Pipelines defined in YAML; example with otlp, batch, otlp and extensions health_check/pprof/zpages (OTW p.3)

deployment_agent_gateway.name: Collector deployment: Agent vs Gateway
deployment_agent_gateway.summary: Agent (on the application host; binary, sidecar, DaemonSet) is the recommended option; Gateway is a standalone service per cluster/datacenter, more complex, with token management and scaling.
rules: Agent: recommended; push or pull; enriches with tags and hardware information (OTW p.3)
Gateway: standalone service, multiple instances, per cluster or datacenter; API token management and scaling flexibility (OTW p.3)
not_in_book: Layered agent+gateway topologies (the text does not describe them)

otlp.name: OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP)
otlp.summary: Specification for encoding, transporting, and delivering telemetry between sources, collectors, and backends; gRPC or HTTP with a Protocol Buffer schema.
rules: Between sources, intermediate nodes, and backends, via gRPC or HTTP with Protocol Buffers (OTW p.3)
not_in_book: Default ports 4317/4318 (4317 only appears in the example YAML)

instrumentation.name: Automatic vs manual instrumentation; legacy
instrumentation.summary: Automatic saves repetitive code but loses control; manual gives control; legacy can use a converter such as Telegraf instead of refactoring.
rules: Instrumenting = adding the SDK to emit signals; automatic and manual options (OTW p.4)
FlaskInstrumentor replaces the manual code; supports Django, MongoDB, PostgreSQL (OTW p.6)
Automatic saves code, but loses control (OTW p.6)
Legacy: refactoring may not be worth it; Telegraf converts existing telemetry to OTel (OTW p.6)
DOW p.6: instrument via code (APM) or service mesh

backends.name: Backends for traces, metrics, and logs
backends.summary: Traces: Zipkin and Jaeger; metrics: InfluxDB and Prometheus; logs: Telegraf/Logstash/FluentD + ElasticSearch; the choice is a trade-off.
rules: Traces: Zipkin and Jaeger (OTW p.7)
Metrics: InfluxDB and Prometheus (OTW p.7)
Logs: conversion to metrics in a TSDB or ElasticSearch; Telegraf/Logstash/FluentD in pre-processing (OTW p.7)
Switching backend = changing the exporter configuration (OTW p.7)
not_in_book: Commercial backends beyond mentions of contributors

platform_considerations.name: Platform considerations checklist
platform_considerations.summary: Ten considerations: HA, scalability, auto discovery, security, distributed storage, cost, compliance, documentation, usability, integration, compatibility.
rules: Ten items with guiding questions in the table (DOW p.5)
A single team does not design the platform (DOW p.5)

how_to_collect.name: How to monitor, log, and trace
how_to_collect.summary: Start with metrics; one agent per system (monitored); centralize in a TSDB; log policy; instrumentation via code/APM or service mesh with a unique identifier per step.
rules: Metrics first: physical, then system (DOW p.5)
One agent per system, monitored, without consuming too much; centralize in a remote platform (DOW p.6)
Global log policy, tags, collector (DOW p.6)
Instrumentation via code (APM) or service mesh; unique identifier per step (DOW p.6)
not_in_book: Agent product names beyond integration examples

graphs_alerts.name: Graphs and alerts
graphs_alerts.summary: Graphs give a global view over time; alerts allow proactive action; without interpretation, observability loses value.
rules: Graphs for the whole organization (DOW p.4)
Alerts on deviant behavior, proactive action (DOW p.4)
Requires collection and interpretation maturity (DOW p.5)

status_2021.name: Specification status in 2021 [DATED]
status_2021.summary: In 2021 only Tracing was stable; Metrics v1.0 expected for the end of 2021; Logs in draft.
rules: Only Tracing stable; Metrics 1.0 expected at the end of 2021; Logs in draft, maybe 2022 (OTW p.4)
not_in_book: Current status of any specification (check current documentation)
